sentence: Original: 'The procedure was revised in response to the panel's advice.' Edit: 'The procedure was revised in accordance with the panel's advice.'
setupText: Choose the editorial assessment that preserves the distinction between responding to advice and following it.
taskText: Original: 'The procedure was revised in response to the panel's advice.' Edit: 'The procedure was revised in accordance with the panel's advice.'
text: Choose the editorial assessment that preserves the distinction between responding to advice and following it. Original: 'The procedure was revised in response to the panel's advice.' Edit: 'The procedure was revised in accordance with the panel's advice.'
options: The edit removes the panel's connection with the revision.
The edit adds that the revision followed the advice, not merely that the advice prompted it.
The edit says the panel itself revised the procedure.
The edit changes completed revision into a proposal for revision.
answer: The edit adds that the revision followed the advice, not merely that the advice prompted it.
focusKey: coverage-prepositions-c1-2601:Prompting versus conformity
explanation: 'In response to' identifies a stimulus; 'in accordance with' additionally presents conformity with the advice.

rationales.The edit adds that the revision followed: 'In response to' identifies a stimulus; 'in accordance with' additionally presents conformity with the advice.
rationales.The edit removes the panel's connection: Both versions retain a relationship to the panel's advice; the kind of relationship changes.
rationales.The edit says the panel itself revised t: Neither prepositional phrase identifies the person who carried out the revision.
rationales.The edit changes completed revision into: Both clauses still report that the procedure was revised; the change concerns conformity, not completion.

sentence: 'The agreement sets out the responsibilities shared between the publisher, the printer, and the distributor.' An editor objects that 'between' cannot refer to three parties.
setupText: Choose the sound editorial judgment about the preposition, without changing the stated relationship.
taskText: 'The agreement sets out the responsibilities shared between the publisher, the printer, and the distributor.' An editor objects that 'between' cannot refer to three parties.
text: Choose the sound editorial judgment about the preposition, without changing the stated relationship. 'The agreement sets out the responsibilities shared between the publisher, the printer, and the distributor.' An editor objects that 'between' cannot refer to three parties.
options: Among is required because between becomes ungrammatical whenever a third party is named.
Between proves that each responsibility belongs jointly to exactly two of the parties.
Among would prove that all three parties have identical responsibilities.
Between is possible because the parties are individually identified; three parties do not make it ungrammatical.
answer: Between is possible because the parties are individually identified; three parties do not make it ungrammatical.
focusKey: coverage-prepositions-c1-2602:Between with multiple distinct parties
explanation: 'Between' can express relationships among separately identified parties. It is not restricted to exactly two.

rationales.Among is required because between become: The number alone does not prohibit 'between'; it can relate three or more distinct parties.
rationales.Between is possible because the parties: 'Between' can express relationships among separately identified parties. It is not restricted to exactly two.
rationales.Between proves that each responsibility: The preposition does not impose a pair-by-pair allocation of responsibilities.
rationales.Among would prove that all three parties: 'Among' would not by itself establish identical duties for everyone.

sentence: The committee placed renewed emphasis on privacy in its review of the software.
setupText: Choose the summary that preserves emphasis without upgrading it to an exclusive priority.
taskText: The committee placed renewed emphasis on privacy in its review of the software.
text: Choose the summary that preserves emphasis without upgrading it to an exclusive priority. The committee placed renewed emphasis on privacy in its review of the software.
options: Privacy replaced usability as the review's sole concern.
The software review was conducted on behalf of privacy campaigners.
Privacy received fresh emphasis during the software review.
The committee's review resulted in stronger privacy protections.
answer: Privacy received fresh emphasis during the software review.
focusKey: coverage-prepositions-c1-2603:Focus on without exclusivity or outcome
explanation: 'Emphasis on' marks a focus of attention; renewed emphasis does not exclude other priorities or specify its comparative amount.

rationales.Privacy replaced usability as the review: An emphasis on privacy does not establish replacement of other concerns or exclusivity.
rationales.The software review was conducted on beh: 'On privacy' names the focus of emphasis, not a group represented by the reviewers.
rationales.Privacy received fresh emphasis during t: 'Emphasis on' marks a focus of attention; renewed emphasis does not exclude other priorities or specify its comparative amount.
rationales.The committee's review resulted in stron: Attention to privacy does not itself establish that protections were changed.

sentence: The agreement gives researchers access to the archive's letters, but the originals remain in the archive.
setupText: An editor wants to distinguish permission to consult letters from possession of the originals. Choose the faithful summary.
taskText: The agreement gives researchers access to the archive's letters, but the originals remain in the archive.
text: An editor wants to distinguish permission to consult letters from possession of the originals. Choose the faithful summary. The agreement gives researchers access to the archive's letters, but the originals remain in the archive.
options: Researchers receive the original letters for their own collections.
Researchers acquire ownership of copies but cannot consult the originals.
Researchers may consult the letters without taking possession of the originals.
Researchers may authorize the archive to dispose of the original letters.
answer: Researchers may consult the letters without taking possession of the originals.
focusKey: coverage-prepositions-c1-2604:Access to versus possession of
explanation: 'Access to' describes availability for consultation here, while the second clause preserves custody.

rationales.Researchers receive the original letters: Access to the letters does not transfer possession, and the originals remain in the archive.
rationales.Researchers may consult the letters with: 'Access to' describes availability for consultation here, while the second clause preserves custody.
rationales.Researchers acquire ownership of copies: The agreement says nothing about ownership of copies and allows access to the letters.
rationales.Researchers may authorize the archive to: Access grants no stated authority over disposal or ownership.

sentence: The report is based on interviews with former tenants.
setupText: Choose the edit that preserves an evidential basis without identifying the people who wrote the report.
taskText: The report is based on interviews with former tenants.
text: Choose the edit that preserves an evidential basis without identifying the people who wrote the report. The report is based on interviews with former tenants.
options: Interviews with former tenants provide the basis for the report.
Former tenants wrote the report on the basis of interviews.
The report provides a basis for interviewing former tenants.
The report is addressed to former tenants who were interviewed.
answer: Interviews with former tenants provide the basis for the report.
focusKey: coverage-prepositions-c1-2605:Evidential basis and embedded participant phrase
explanation: 'Based on' identifies supporting material; 'with former tenants' identifies the interview participants.

rationales.Former tenants wrote the report on the b: This turns interview participants into authors, which the original does not establish.
rationales.The report provides a basis for intervie: This reverses the direction: the interviews support the report, not the report the interviews.
rationales.The report is addressed to former tenant: This changes participants in the evidence into the report's intended audience.
rationales.Interviews with former tenants provide t: 'Based on' identifies supporting material; 'with former tenants' identifies the interview participants.

sentence: Aisha spoke on behalf of the residents, some of whom opposed the proposal she presented.
setupText: Choose the interpretation that distinguishes representation from support for a policy.
taskText: Aisha spoke on behalf of the residents, some of whom opposed the proposal she presented.
text: Choose the interpretation that distinguishes representation from support for a policy. Aisha spoke on behalf of the residents, some of whom opposed the proposal she presented.
options: Aisha spoke in favour of the proposal because the residents had unanimously endorsed it.
Aisha represented the residents, including opponents of the proposal.
Aisha replaced the residents' proposal with one that she personally preferred.
Aisha spoke about the residents rather than representing them.
answer: Aisha represented the residents, including opponents of the proposal.
focusKey: coverage-prepositions-c1-2606:Representation on behalf of versus endorsement
explanation: 'On behalf of' expresses representation. Residents who opposed the proposal could still be included in the group represented.

rationales.Aisha spoke in favour of the proposal be: 'On behalf of' names whom she represented; the second clause rules out unanimous support.
rationales.Aisha replaced the residents' proposal w: Representation does not establish substitution of a proposal or Aisha's personal preference.
rationales.Aisha represented the residents, includi: 'On behalf of' expresses representation. Residents who opposed the proposal could still be included in the group represented.
rationales.Aisha spoke about the residents rather t: Speaking about a group would make it the topic; 'on behalf of' assigns a representative role.

sentence: Original: 'In contrast to the earlier policy, the new policy covers temporary staff.' Edit: 'Contrary to the earlier policy, the new policy covers temporary staff.'
setupText: Choose the assessment of the change in relationship, not a claim about which policy is better.
taskText: Original: 'In contrast to the earlier policy, the new policy covers temporary staff.' Edit: 'Contrary to the earlier policy, the new policy covers temporary staff.'
text: Choose the assessment of the change in relationship, not a claim about which policy is better. Original: 'In contrast to the earlier policy, the new policy covers temporary staff.' Edit: 'Contrary to the earlier policy, the new policy covers temporary staff.'
options: The edit merely shortens the wording while preserving a neutral comparison.
The edit presents coverage as conflicting with the earlier policy, rather than simply contrasting the policies.
The edit says the earlier policy caused the new coverage.
The edit changes temporary staff from beneficiaries into the writers of the policy.
answer: The edit presents coverage as conflicting with the earlier policy, rather than simply contrasting the policies.
focusKey: coverage-prepositions-c1-2607:Neutral contrast versus conflict
explanation: Changing 'in contrast to' to 'contrary to' adds an oppositional relationship, not just a comparison.

rationales.The edit merely shortens the wording whi: 'Contrary to' presents opposition or inconsistency; 'in contrast to' can simply compare a difference.
rationales.The edit says the earlier policy caused: Neither phrase expresses causation by the earlier policy.
rationales.The edit presents coverage as conflictin: Changing 'in contrast to' to 'contrary to' adds an oppositional relationship, not just a comparison.
rationales.The edit changes temporary staff from be: The staff remain those covered; the edit changes the relationship between policies.

sentence: Ambiguous draft: 'The journalist photographed the visitor with a borrowed camera.'
setupText: Choose the revision that clearly makes the camera the journalist's tool, not something the visitor possessed.
taskText: Ambiguous draft: 'The journalist photographed the visitor with a borrowed camera.'
text: Choose the revision that clearly makes the camera the journalist's tool, not something the visitor possessed. Ambiguous draft: 'The journalist photographed the visitor with a borrowed camera.'
options: Using a borrowed camera, the journalist photographed the visitor.
The journalist photographed the visitor who had a borrowed camera.
The visitor with a borrowed camera was photographed by the journalist.
The journalist photographed a visitor's borrowed camera.
answer: Using a borrowed camera, the journalist photographed the visitor.
focusKey: coverage-prepositions-c1-2608:Instrument versus noun attachment of with
explanation: Moving the instrument phrase to a clause about the journalist makes its role explicit.

rationales.The journalist photographed the visitor: This assigns the camera to the visitor, the reading the edit must avoid.
rationales.Using a borrowed camera, the journalist: Moving the instrument phrase to a clause about the journalist makes its role explicit.
rationales.The visitor with a borrowed camera was p: This attaches the camera phrase to the visitor and preserves the unwanted reading.
rationales.The journalist photographed a visitor's: This makes the camera the photographed object rather than the instrument.

sentence: The voucher is valid for travel within the city, but not for journeys beyond its boundary.
setupText: Choose the summary that preserves both the restriction and the possibility left open.
taskText: The voucher is valid for travel within the city, but not for journeys beyond its boundary.
text: Choose the summary that preserves both the restriction and the possibility left open. The voucher is valid for travel within the city, but not for journeys beyond its boundary.
options: It covers trips that begin inside the city, wherever they end.
It covers journeys towards the city but not journeys away from it.
It covers only trips along the city's outer boundary.
It covers travel inside the city, not trips extending outside it.
answer: It covers travel inside the city, not trips extending outside it.
focusKey: coverage-prepositions-c1-2609:Geographical extent within and beyond
explanation: 'Within' sets a geographical limit, reinforced by the exclusion of travel beyond it.

rationales.It covers trips that begin inside the ci: This ignores the exclusion of journeys beyond the city's boundary.
rationales.It covers journeys towards the city but: Direction is not the stated criterion; geographical limits are.
rationales.It covers travel inside the city, not tr: 'Within' sets a geographical limit, reinforced by the exclusion of travel beyond it.
rationales.It covers only trips along the city's ou: 'Within' includes the interior; it does not restrict travel to the boundary itself.

sentence: The editor reopened the inquiry ___ the newly discovered letters.
setupText: Choose the phrase that presents the new evidence as a reason to reconsider, not as something disregarded.
taskText: The editor reopened the inquiry ___ the newly discovered letters.
text: Choose the phrase that presents the new evidence as a reason to reconsider, not as something disregarded. The editor reopened the inquiry ___ the newly discovered letters.
options: regardless of
in spite of
in light of
in the absence of
answer: in light of
focusKey: coverage-prepositions-c1-2610:Evidential consideration in light of
explanation: 'In light of' means taking the letters into account as grounds for reconsideration.

rationales.regardless of: This makes the decision independent of the letters rather than responsive to their evidential significance.
rationales.in light of: 'In light of' means taking the letters into account as grounds for reconsideration.
rationales.in spite of: This presents the letters as a possible obstacle to reopening, not the stated reason.
rationales.in the absence of: This presents the letters as unavailable, not as evidence taken into account in reopening the inquiry.

sentence: The team met with a view to reducing delays.
setupText: Choose the edit that preserves the review's intended aim without saying the aim was achieved.
taskText: The team met with a view to reducing delays.
text: Choose the edit that preserves the review's intended aim without saying the aim was achieved. The team met with a view to reducing delays.
options: The team met with the aim of reducing delays.
The team met as a result of reduced delays.
The team met after reducing delays.
The team met and thereby reduced delays.
answer: The team met with the aim of reducing delays.
focusKey: coverage-prepositions-c1-2611:Prospective purpose with a view to
explanation: 'With a view to' expresses an aim and takes a noun or gerund complement; it does not guarantee success.

rationales.The team met as a result of reduced dela: This turns an intended result into an already achieved cause of the meeting.
rationales.The team met with the aim of reducing de: 'With a view to' expresses an aim and takes a noun or gerund complement; it does not guarantee success.
This makes the reduction an earlier event rather than the meeting's purpose.
'Thereby' claims an achieved result, which the purpose phrase does not establish.

sentence: For a first-time presenter, Leo handled the questions confidently.
setupText: Choose the reading that keeps the comparison's reference group.
taskText: For a first-time presenter, Leo handled the questions confidently.
text: Choose the reading that keeps the comparison's reference group. For a first-time presenter, Leo handled the questions confidently.
options: Leo handled the questions on behalf of another first-time presenter.
Leo became confident because another first-time presenter helped him.
Leo handled only questions intended for first-time presenters.
Leo's handling of questions was confident when judged against expectations for a first-time presenter.
answer: Leo's handling of questions was confident when judged against expectations for a first-time presenter.
focusKey: coverage-prepositions-c1-2612:Evaluative reference frame introduced by for
explanation: Initial 'for a first-time presenter' qualifies the evaluation by naming the relevant comparison group.

rationales.Leo handled the questions on behalf of a: 'For' here sets the standard of comparison; it does not assign a representative role.
rationales.Leo became confident because another fir: The phrase supplies a comparison frame, not a cause or helper.
rationales.Leo's handling of questions was confiden: Initial 'for a first-time presenter' qualifies the evaluation by naming the relevant comparison group.
rationales.Leo handled only questions intended for: The initial phrase evaluates Leo; it does not restrict which questions were asked.

sentence: Which revision preserves both facts?
setupText: Choose the version matching this editing brief: the museum changed the label at the artist's request; the artist did not write the new text.
taskText: Which revision preserves both facts?
text: Choose the version matching this editing brief: the museum changed the label at the artist's request; the artist did not write the new text. Which revision preserves both facts?
options: By the artist's hand, the museum label was rewritten.
At the artist's request, the museum rewrote the label.
On the artist's behalf, the museum displayed the artist's new label.
With the artist's permission, the museum commissioned a new label.
answer: At the artist's request, the museum rewrote the label.
focusKey: coverage-prepositions-c1-2613:Requesting party versus authorizing party and agent
explanation: 'At someone's request' identifies the prompt for an action without making that person its agent.

rationales.By the artist's hand, the museum label w: This attributes the writing to the artist, contrary to the brief.
rationales.At the artist's request, the museum rewr: 'At someone's request' identifies the prompt for an action without making that person its agent.
rationales.On the artist's behalf, the museum displ: This adds artist authorship and changes rewriting into displaying.
rationales.With the artist's permission, the museum: Permission is not the same as a request, and commissioning does not preserve who rewrote it.

sentence: Original: 'The article contains criticism of the agency.' Edit: 'The article contains criticism by the agency.'
setupText: In the original, 'of' names the target of the criticism. Choose the assessment of what the edit changes.
taskText: Original: 'The article contains criticism of the agency.' Edit: 'The article contains criticism by the agency.'
text: In the original, 'of' names the target of the criticism. Choose the assessment of what the edit changes. Original: 'The article contains criticism of the agency.' Edit: 'The article contains criticism by the agency.'
options: The edit preserves the target but makes the criticism more severe.
The edit says the agency commissioned the article but did not supply criticism.
The edit makes the agency the source of criticism instead of its target.
The edit narrows criticism of the agency to criticism of its director.
answer: The edit makes the agency the source of criticism instead of its target.
focusKey: coverage-prepositions-c1-2614:Criticism of target versus by source
explanation: With 'criticism', 'of the agency' identifies what is criticized; 'by the agency' identifies who voices it.

rationales.The edit preserves the target but makes: Changing 'of' to 'by' changes a participant's role, not the degree of criticism.
rationales.The edit says the agency commissioned th: 'Criticism by the agency' attributes the criticism to it; commissioning is not stated.
rationales.The edit makes the agency the source of: With 'criticism', 'of the agency' identifies what is criticized; 'by the agency' identifies who voices it.
rationales.The edit narrows criticism of the agency: Neither phrase singles out the director; the change is source versus target.

sentence: The editor set the account aside for want of corroboration, not because it had been disproved.
setupText: Choose the summary that preserves the stated reason for setting aside the account without treating lack of support as proof of falsity.
taskText: The editor set the account aside for want of corroboration, not because it had been disproved.
text: Choose the summary that preserves the stated reason for setting aside the account without treating lack of support as proof of falsity. The editor set the account aside for want of corroboration, not because it had been disproved.
options: The account was set aside in order to obtain proof that it was false.
The account was set aside despite having received independent confirmation.
The account was set aside pending the expected arrival of confirmation.
The account was set aside because supporting confirmation was lacking.
answer: The account was set aside because supporting confirmation was lacking.
focusKey: coverage-prepositions-c1-2615:For want of as deficiency cause rather than disproof or purpose
explanation: 'For want of' means because of a lack of something. The final clause distinguishes missing support from disproof.

rationales.The account was set aside in order to ob: 'For want of' identifies an existing lack; it does not express a purpose of disproving the account.
rationales.The account was set aside because suppor: 'For want of' means because of a lack of something. The final clause distinguishes missing support from disproof.
rationales.The account was set aside despite having: This changes lack of corroboration into its presence and replaces a cause with a concession.
rationales.The account was set aside pending the ex: 'Pending' would present a temporary waiting state and expected event, neither of which the original specifies.

sentence: The witness's account conflicts with the station log.
setupText: Choose the formal revision that identifies an inconsistency between two accounts without saying which is true.
taskText: The witness's account conflicts with the station log.
text: Choose the formal revision that identifies an inconsistency between two accounts without saying which is true. The witness's account conflicts with the station log.
options: The witness's account is at variance with the station log.
The witness's account takes precedence over the station log.
The witness's account is derived from the station log.
The witness's account is verified against the station log.
answer: The witness's account is at variance with the station log.
focusKey: coverage-prepositions-c1-2616:Inconsistency at variance with versus evidential priority
explanation: 'At variance with' expresses inconsistency without deciding which source should be accepted.

rationales.The witness's account takes precedence o: This gives the account priority or authority instead of simply reporting a conflict.
rationales.The witness's account is at variance wit: 'At variance with' expresses inconsistency without deciding which source should be accepted.
rationales.The witness's account is derived from th: This identifies the log as the account's source, not an inconsistent account to compare it with.
rationales.The witness's account is verified agains: This describes checking the account using the log; it does not preserve the finding that they conflict.

sentence: A dialogue contains: 'Which proposal were you referring to?' An editor wants to remove the final 'to' because sentences should not end with a preposition.
setupText: Choose the editorial advice that preserves a natural conversational question.
taskText: A dialogue contains: 'Which proposal were you referring to?' An editor wants to remove the final 'to' because sentences should not end with a preposition.
text: Choose the editorial advice that preserves a natural conversational question. A dialogue contains: 'Which proposal were you referring to?' An editor wants to remove the final 'to' because sentences should not end with a preposition.
options: Delete to; referring takes the proposal as a direct object in this meaning.
Keep to: refer to needs it here, and a final preposition is natural in this dialogue.
Replace to with about because final to is not allowed in direct questions.
Move to before which because only indirect questions permit a final preposition.
answer: Keep to: refer to needs it here, and a final preposition is natural in this dialogue.
focusKey: coverage-prepositions-c1-2617:Preposition stranding in conversational questions
explanation: Preposition stranding is normal in English questions. 'To which proposal were you referring?' is possible but more formal.

rationales.Delete to; referring takes the proposal: For mentioning or alluding to a proposal, the construction is 'refer to', not 'refer a proposal'.
rationales.Keep to: refer to needs it here, and a f: Preposition stranding is normal in English questions. 'To which proposal were you referring?' is possible but more formal.
rationales.Replace to with about because final to i: The position is allowed, and 'referring about' is not the required construction.
rationales.Move to before which because only indire: Direct questions also allow final prepositions; fronting is a style choice here, not a grammatical requirement.

sentence: The new study proceeds ___ the assumption that remote work reduces collaboration.
setupText: Choose the phrase that says the researcher is examining the assumption critically, not using it as an accepted starting point.
taskText: The new study proceeds ___ the assumption that remote work reduces collaboration.
text: Choose the phrase that says the researcher is examining the assumption critically, not using it as an accepted starting point. The new study proceeds ___ the assumption that remote work reduces collaboration.
options: on
from
in accordance with
by questioning
answer: by questioning
focusKey: coverage-prepositions-c1-2618:Accepted premise versus method of questioning
explanation: 'By questioning' identifies critical examination as the method of proceeding.

rationales.on: 'Proceeds on the assumption' takes it as a starting premise rather than examining it critically.
rationales.from: 'Proceeds from the assumption' also treats it as a basis for further work.
rationales.by questioning: 'By questioning' identifies critical examination as the method of proceeding.
rationales.in accordance with: This presents the study as following the assumption, not challenging it.

sentence: The report describes the risk to historic buildings from heavy traffic.
setupText: Choose the interpretation that does not confuse the object of risk with its source.
taskText: The report describes the risk to historic buildings from heavy traffic.
text: Choose the interpretation that does not confuse the object of risk with its source. The report describes the risk to historic buildings from heavy traffic.
options: Historic buildings are presented as a threat to heavy traffic.
The report treats historic buildings as a means of reducing heavy traffic.
Heavy traffic is presented as a threat to the historic buildings.
The report identifies heavy traffic as a result of damage to historic buildings.
answer: Heavy traffic is presented as a threat to the historic buildings.
focusKey: coverage-prepositions-c1-2619:Threatened object to and risk source from
explanation: 'Risk to' names what is endangered; 'from' identifies the source of that danger.

rationales.Historic buildings are presented as a th: This reverses the threatened thing and the threat's source.
rationales.Heavy traffic is presented as a threat t: 'Risk to' names what is endangered; 'from' identifies the source of that danger.
rationales.The report treats historic buildings as: A risk relation does not describe a traffic-reduction measure.
rationales.The report identifies heavy traffic as a: This turns a potential source of harm into an effect of damage, which the sentence does not say.

sentence: Questions about staff pay fall outside the scope of this safety review.
setupText: Choose the interpretation that keeps the limitation on the review's remit, not on whether a problem exists.
taskText: Questions about staff pay fall outside the scope of this safety review.
text: Choose the interpretation that keeps the limitation on the review's remit, not on whether a problem exists. Questions about staff pay fall outside the scope of this safety review.
options: This review does not cover staff pay, whether or not pay issues exist.
The review has established that staff pay presents no problems.
Staff pay will be reviewed after the safety work is finished.
Staff pay is too difficult for any review to address.
answer: This review does not cover staff pay, whether or not pay issues exist.
focusKey: coverage-prepositions-c1-2620:Scope exclusion versus a negative finding
explanation: 'Outside the scope of' limits the subjects examined; it does not make a finding about excluded subjects.

rationales.The review has established that staff pa: Excluding a subject from a review does not establish that the subject is problem-free.
rationales.Staff pay will be reviewed after the saf: 'Outside the scope' does not schedule a later review.
rationales.Staff pay is too difficult for any revie: The limitation concerns this review's remit, not what any review could handle.
rationales.This review does not cover staff pay, wh: 'Outside the scope of' limits the subjects examined; it does not make a finding about excluded subjects.
